about.privacy.intro: WEblok collects and stores only the data needed to run the service - nothing more. This page explains, in plain language, what is stored, how it's protected, and why.
about.privacy.dataBody: Your name, email, and account role (user/admin), the blocks and projects you've saved, and messages sent through the contact form. That's it.
about.privacy.keysBody: If you choose to store an API key on the server, it is encrypted before storage - nobody, including us, can read it as plain text from the database. You can also choose to keep it in your browser only, so it never reaches our server.
about.privacy.rlsBody: The database is built so each user can only see and touch their own data - enforced at the database level itself, not just in the website's design, so even a code bug can't expose someone else's data.
about.privacy.openSourceBody: The site's source code is publicly visible on GitHub. It never includes personal information or secrets - keys and passwords always live outside the code itself.
about.privacy.contact: Questions about privacy? Reach out through the contact form on the site.
about.accessibility.intro: WEblok places great importance on making the site accessible to the general public, including people with disabilities. We work to keep the site accessible, clear, and easy to use for everyone.
about.accessibility.levelBody: The site is built following the recommendations of WCAG 2.1 level AA by the W3C.
about.accessibility.a1: The site is responsive - suited for desktop, tablet, and mobile.
about.accessibility.a3: Headings used for content structure and hierarchy.
about.accessibility.a5: Adequate color contrast, in both dark and light mode.
about.accessibility.contactBody: We keep working to improve the site's accessibility. If you run into an issue or have a suggestion, we'd love to hear from you - through the contact form on the site.

inject.title: Inject into existing project
inject.subtitle: Upload your site's HTML file, pick a block, and the AI adds it in the right place - without touching the rest of your code. Everything happens in your browser: the file is never uploaded to our server.
inject.step1: Upload one HTML file from your site (e.g. index.html).
inject.step2: Pick the blocks to add - with default settings, or as you designed them in the editor.
inject.step3: Enter a personal Gemini key (not stored on any server) and describe where the block should go - or choose simple injection without AI.
inject.step4: Check the before/after preview and download the updated file.
inject.privacyBody: The file is read and edited only in your browser and is never sent to WEblok's server. With AI injection, the file and blocks are sent directly from your browser to Google Gemini using your key, under Google's terms. We never store the key.

structures.title: Structures
structures.subtitle: Complete, deploy-ready projects - not an embeddable block but a full site with a server and a database. Design it here, push to GitHub (or download a ZIP) and deploy on your own Vercel. Everything runs on your side - we never see the data.
structures.privacy: The editor runs only in your browser. Your settings, image and GitHub token are never sent to WEblok's server, and the finished site runs on your own Vercel and Supabase - we have no access to guests or replies.
structures.previewNote: A static rendering of the invitation page. Submitting, the admin page and the data work on the deployed site.
structures.draftNote: Your draft is saved in this browser only (without the image).
structures.resetConfirm: Reset all settings to the defaults?
structures.zipText: All project files in one archive - for uploading to GitHub manually.
structures.ghText: Creates a new repo (or updates an existing one) straight from your browser, with your own token.
structures.why.own.title: Fully yours
structures.why.own.text: The code lives in your GitHub, the site on your Vercel and the data in your Supabase. Edit, extend or move it freely.
structures.why.safe.title: Secure out of the box
structures.why.safe.text: RLS with no public access, server-only keys, signed admin sessions, rate limiting and a strict CSP.
structures.why.fast.title: Live in 10 minutes
structures.why.fast.text: The free tiers of Supabase and Vercel are enough. Every structure comes with a step-by-step guide.
structures.rsvp.name: Event RSVP system
structures.rsvp.description: A digital invitation with an RSVP form, Waze and Google Maps directions, add-to-calendar and a secure admin page with totals and Excel export.
structures.rsvp.f.eyebrowHint: Empty = based on the event type (e.g. "Wedding").

structures.secrets.title: Admin page secrets
structures.secrets.text: The owner signs in to /admin with a password that is set only in Vercel - it never goes into the code. You can generate strong values here (created in your browser and never stored) and copy them to the environment variables.
structures.secrets.note: Keep the password somewhere safe (e.g. a password manager). The values disappear when you refresh the page.
structures.guide.title: Export & deployment guide
structures.guide.subtitle: About 10 minutes, on the free tiers of Supabase and Vercel. The same guide is included in the project's README.md.
structures.guide.design.title: Design and check the preview
structures.guide.design.text: Fill in the event details, location and design. You can upload the invitation or a photo of the couple as the background and tune the overlay so the text stays readable.
structures.guide.supabase.title: Create a Supabase database
structures.guide.supabase.text:
On supabase.com → New project. Then SQL Editor → New query → paste the contents of supabase/schema.sql → Run.
In Project Settings → API copy the Project URL and the Secret key (or service_role on older projects).
structures.guide.github.title: Get the code into GitHub
structures.guide.github.text: Easiest: use "Push to GitHub" above (new repo, private recommended). Or download the ZIP, create a repo and upload the files via Add file → Upload files.
structures.guide.vercel.title: Deploy on Vercel
structures.guide.vercel.text: On vercel.com/new import the repo. Before Deploy, open Environment Variables and add four variables:
structures.guide.env.secret: The Secret key from Supabase - secret, server only
structures.guide.env.session: A random 32+ character string for signing the cookie
structures.guide.test.title: Test it
structures.guide.test.text: Open the address Vercel gave you and send a test RSVP. Go to /admin with your password - the reply shows up there, with attendance totals and Excel export. You can delete the test reply.
structures.guide.share.title: Share with guests and update
structures.guide.share.text: Send the link over WhatsApp or SMS (you can connect your own domain in Vercel). To change details later, edit config/event.json on GitHub and Vercel updates the site automatically.
structures.security.title: Security & privacy
structures.security.subtitle: What stays with you: everything. What stays with us: nothing.
structures.security.where.title: Where everything lives:
structures.security.where.text: The code in your GitHub, the site on your Vercel, and guests and replies in your Supabase.
structures.security.weblok.title: What WEblok keeps:
structures.security.weblok.text: Nothing. The editor runs in your browser, the image is never uploaded, your GitHub token goes straight to GitHub, and we have no connection to the finished site.
structures.security.db.title: Database:
structures.security.db.text: RLS is on with no public access - nothing can be read or written from the browser. Only the server, with the secret key stored only in Vercel, touches the data.
structures.security.admin.title: Admin page:
structures.security.admin.text: Password from an environment variable, constant-time comparison, 5 attempts per 15 minutes, and a signed (HMAC) httpOnly + Secure + SameSite=Strict cookie for eight hours.
structures.security.form.title: RSVP form:
structures.security.form.text: Server-side validation of every field, a request size cap, a bot trap, per-IP rate limiting (only a hash is stored), CSRF protection and a strict CSP that blocks foreign servers.
structures.security.you.title: Your part:
structures.security.you.text: Use a strong password, never share the secret key (if it leaks, rotate it in Supabase right away), and delete the data after the event.
